description: WORKED EXAMPLE: exercises the graph executor with the real `wc` word-count command. A `shell` node runs `wc -w` on a document; a `decide` node classifies the document SHORT/MEDIUM/LONG; the graph routes on that label. TWO THINGS ARE DELIBERATE. (1) The decision is deterministic: the classification rule is stated in the prompt together with the exact word count, so the model is not guessing. (2) The count in the prompt is a LITERAL, copied from `wc`'s real output by hand -- the engine has NO interpolation, so the shell node's output does not flow into the decide node's state. That limitation is the finding, documented in /projects/_tmp/wc-example/REPORT.md, not a bug: `decide.prompt` is forwarded verbatim (crates/laya-graph/src/lower.rs:104) and a `route` may only follow an `mcp` node (crates/laya-graph/src/route_exec.rs:68-75). Its pairing control is wc-classify.control.flow.json: the identical graph shape over a longer document, which must land on a DIFFERENT label.

nodes.prompt: A shell command counted the words in a document. It printed: `13 /projects/_tmp/wc-example/short-note.txt`. The document therefore has 13 words. Classification rule: SHORT = fewer than 100 words; MEDIUM = 100 to 300 words; LONG = more than 300 words. The document has 13 words.
nodes.question: By the rule stated, is this document SHORT, MEDIUM or LONG?
